change.title: pr-10
change.description: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding
change.author: Robin Ward

findings.title: Migration crashes when site_settings has no embed_category / uncategorized_category_id row
findings.body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` is called on the result of a join against the `embed_category` setting. `site_settings` only holds rows for values that were changed, so on any site that never set `embed_category` the result is empty, `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The migration aborts and the deploy fails. Line 15 has the same problem for `uncategorized_category_id`, which may also have no row. Check for an empty result before indexing, and fall back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` or a direct `categories` lookup. Also, the join is on the category name (`s.value = c.name`), which is not unique-safe, so use `LIMIT 1`.

findings.title: Unescaped values interpolated into INSERT; hosts not normalized
findings.body: Each line of the old setting is interpolated into the SQL as `'#{h}'`. A value containing a quote breaks the migration, and it is an injection vector. Lines are also not stripped of `\r` or whitespace, and entries like `http://x.com` or `https://example.com/1234` are inserted without the scheme and path trimming the model does, so `host_allowed?` never matches them. Use `connection.quote`, or create records through SQL after stripping the scheme and path.

findings.title: before_validation raises on nil host; controllers raise 500 instead of validation errors
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil. A POST that omits `embeddable_host[host]` gives a 500 instead of a validation error. It is also an in-place mutation. Use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`, or guard for nil. Separately, the format regex accepts `:port`, but `record_for_host` compares against `URI#host`, which has no port, and does not downcase. A host stored with a port or capitals can never match.

findings.title: Missing record or params give a 500
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` use `.where(id:).first`, which returns nil for an unknown id, so `host.destroy` and `save_host(nil)` raise NoMethodError. Use `find` (404) or `raise Discourse::NotFound`. `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` at line 23 also raises if the key is missing; use `params.require`.

findings.title: update action is a no-op
findings.body: `update` only re-serializes, and the client's `saveChanges` calls `update({})`. Nothing is persisted. If it is a placeholder, remove it or document it.

findings.title: Fabricator contents swapped between files
findings.body: The category fabricators moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`, and `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `:embeddable_host`. It works because all fabricators are loaded, but the file names are misleading and the diff is noisy. Keep each fabricator in its matching file.

findings.title: Test name no longer matches what it checks
findings.body: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now passes only because `has_topic_embed?` is false. `expandable_first_post?` no longer looks at hosts (app/models/topic.rb:869). Rename or drop the test. The block title also has a typo, "emeddable".

findings.title: Broadened regex affects every REST model with *_ids keys
findings.body: `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` now applies to all store types. Any payload with a key such as `foo_ids` is deleted and replaced by a pluralized hydrated array, with `undefined` entries when a sub-record is missing. `hydrated || []` is dead, because `map` always returns an array. Have you checked existing `*_ids` attributes in other REST models?

contracts.action: Admin adds, edits or deletes an embeddable host
contracts.before_after: Before, the setting was a newline list validated by host_list. Now each host is a record, and the server strips the scheme and path in before_validation.
contracts.visible_effect: The row updates on success, and the error popup shows on failure. Delete removes the row after destroyRecord resolves.
contracts.failure_mode: The delete promise has no catch, so a failed destroy is silent. Server-side nil lookups give a 500, which popupAjaxError shows on save.

contracts.action: Migration deletes the old site settings and copies their values
contracts.before_after: The DELETE removes only the two named settings. If the earlier steps raise, the migration is rolled back in a transaction, so the settings stay.
contracts.visible_effect: Existing embed hosts are migrated, or the migration fails.
contracts.failure_mode: Crashes on missing setting rows (line 11/15). If the INSERT escapes badly the data is lost or the migration fails.

summary: The migration will crash on most installs: it indexes an empty result for the `embed_category` and `uncategorized_category_id` settings, and it interpolates host values into SQL unescaped. The admin controllers and the model's `before_validation` raise 500s on nil records or params. The rest is cleanup: swapped fabricator files, a misnamed topic spec, and a broadened `_ids` regex in the store that I couldn't confirm is safe. The `embed_controller` and `topic_retriever` call-site changes look fine.
